title: ADPKD in Children vs Nephronophthisis: Corticomedullary Cysts and Ciliopathy Overlap
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology
module: Tubulopathies, Polycystic Kidney Disease and Ciliopathies

steps.say: Dominant polycystic disease stems from distinct gene defects governing polycystin complex assembly.
steps.tx: Contrast genetic drivers and renal timelines comparing **ADPKD PKD1 vs PKD2 genes** during family genetic counseling. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease results from mutations in PKD1 on chromosome 16p13.3 (85% of families, encoding polycystin-1, reaching ESRD at a median age 54) or PKD2 on chromosome 4q21 (15% of families, encoding polycystin-2, reaching ESRD at a median age 74).

left.title: PKD1 Mutation (16p13.3)
points: More severe with median ESRD at age 54

right.title: PKD2 Mutation (4q21)
points: Milder progression with median ESRD at age 74

steps.say: Even a solitary macroscopic cyst carries definitive diagnostic predictive power in young at-risk children.
steps.tx: Evaluate familial offspring using revised **Pediatric ADPKD ultrasound diagnostic criteria** on screening sonography. In at-risk children < 15 years with an affected first-degree relative, the presence of >= 1 renal cyst of any size in either kidney has a positive predictive value > 95% for ADPKD, confirming early heterozygous transmission without requiring bilateral involvement.

steps.say: Targeted vasopressin receptor antagonism impedes intracellular cyclic AMP to retard cyst enlargement.
steps.tx: Inhibit cystogenesis in rapidly progressive adolescents utilizing **Tolvaptan V2 receptor antagonist approval** under strict guidance. Tolvaptan, an oral selective V2 receptor antagonist, slows total kidney volume (TKV) expansion and retards eGFR decline by inhibiting intracellular cAMP generation in collecting ducts, approved specifically in adolescents with confirmed rapidly progressive ADPKD phenotype.

nodes.label: cAMP Surges & Drives Tubular Fluid Secretion
Slows Total Kidney Volume & Preserves eGFR

steps.say: Nephronophthisis represents the leading monogenic cause of pediatric kidney failure and maps to primary cilia.
steps.tx: Investigate juvenile tubulointerstitial failure evaluating **Nephronophthisis (NPHP) genetics and ESRD timeline** across pediatric age groups. Nephronophthisis is an autosomal recessive ciliopathy and the most common monogenic cause of pediatric ESRD; homozygous NPHP1 deletions on chromosome 2q13 account for 20-25% of juvenile cases, relentlessly reaching ESRD at a median age 13 years.

vis.title: Juvenile Nephronophthisis Genetic Profile
rows: Median age 13 years requiring dialysis or transplant

steps.say: Renal sonography in nephronophthisis shows shrunken kidneys with microscopic cysts hugging the corticomedullary junction.
steps.tx: Differentiate nephronophthisis from polycystic enlargement identifying the **Nephronophthisis ultrasound tri-hallmark** on imaging. Ultrasonography reveals normal or small-sized kidneys with increased parenchymal echogenicity, loss of corticomedullary differentiation, and characteristic cysts localized exclusively to the corticomedullary junction, distinguishing this fibrosing ciliopathy from the massively enlarged bilateral nephromegaly characteristic of infantile ARPKD or ADPKD.

left.title: Nephronophthisis Sonography
points: Increased echogenicity with lost corticomedullary boundary
Cysts restricted strictly to corticomedullary junction

right.title: ADPKD / ARPKD Sonography
points: Diffuse parenchymal microcysts or macroscopic cysts

steps.say: Defective medullary concentrating capacity generates severe polyuria alongside profound normocytic anemia.
steps.tx: Recognize insidious clinical presentation characterized by **Polyuria, polydipsia and anemia out of proportion** in school-aged children. Affected children present with severely impaired urinary concentrating ability manifesting as polyuria, polydipsia, and secondary enuresis, salt wasting, and normocytic anemia disproportionately severe for their modest level of early renal dysfunction due to blunted peritubular erythropoietin synthesis.

vis.title: Clinical Manifestations of Tubulointerstitial Nephronophthisis
rows: Early interstitial destruction of erythropoietin-producing cells

steps.say: Syndromic ciliopathies couple tubulointerstitial fibrosis with degenerative retinal pigmentary blindness.
steps.tx: Perform comprehensive neuro-ophthalmological screening to detect the **Senior-Loken syndrome ciliopathy association** in affected families. Senior-Loken syndrome pairs nephronophthisis with tapetoretinal degeneration (retinitis pigmentosa or Leber congenital amaurosis), diagnosed definitively by electroretinography showing absent photoreceptor responses, linking shared ciliary axonemal machinery across both renal tubular and retinal photoreceptor cells.

steps.say: Midbrain structural dysplasia producing the molar tooth sign reveals complex central ciliopathy syndromes.
steps.tx: Evaluate neurodevelopmental abnormalities and obtain neuroimaging to recognize **Joubert syndrome molar tooth sign** pathology. Joubert syndrome associates NPHP with cerebellar vermis hypoplasia (manifesting as the classic molar tooth sign on axial brain MRI), neonatal episodic tachypnea/apnea, ataxia, oculomotor apraxia, and global developmental delay, reflecting generalized basal body and primary ciliary dysfunction.

vis.title: Joubert Syndrome Systemic Manifestations
rows: Molar tooth sign on axial MRI
